zones.name: Khuddaka Nikāya
zones.subtitle: the minor collection
zones.blurb: The most heterogeneous basket — Dhammapada and Jātaka to technical exegesis. Its membership is itself disputed: 15 books, 17 with the hermeneutic manuals, 18 once the Burmese Sixth Council admits the Milindapañha.

zones.name: Abhidhamma Piṭaka
zones.subtitle: the basket of higher doctrine
zones.blurb: The systematic analysis of experience into ultimate constituents (dhammas), culminating in the vast Paṭṭhāna. Only two books have worldwide-PD translations; the Yamaka has no standard English at all.

zones.name: Paracanon & Commentary
zones.subtitle: beyond the three baskets
zones.blurb: Works revered but outside (or at the edge of) the Tipiṭaka — Buddhaghosa’s summa, the King Milinda dialogue, the hermeneutic guides, the chronicles, and the classical commentaries that frame how the canon is read.

chips.name: Visuddhimagga
chips.note: Pe Maung Tin →2043; Ñāṇamoli © — no PD yet

zones.name: Sūtra 經
zones.subtitle: the discourses
zones.blurb: The nine sūtra divisions — from the Āgamas (parallels of the Pāli Nikāyas) through the great Mahāyāna scriptures.

zones.name: Esoteric 密教部
zones.subtitle: tantra / mikkyō
zones.blurb: The esoteric division — the scriptural base of Shingon and Tendai mikkyō, plus a vast body of dhāraṇī texts.

zones.name: Vinaya 律部
zones.subtitle: monastic discipline
zones.blurb: Five complete Vinaya codes; the Dharmaguptaka is the basis of all East Asian ordination.

zones.name: Śāstra 論
zones.subtitle: treatises
zones.blurb: The Indian treatise tradition in Chinese — Abhidharma, Madhyamaka, Yogācāra — plus the collection holding the Awakening of Faith.

zones.name: Commentaries & Schools 諸宗部
zones.subtitle: exegesis & sects
zones.blurb: The Chinese/Japanese exegetical layer, then the "schools" — Tiantai, Huayan, Chan/Zen, Pure Land.

zones.name: History, Reference & Beyond
zones.subtitle: vols 49–85
zones.blurb: The non-scriptural remainder — travel records, biographies, encyclopedias, catalogs, the Japanese sub-commentary block, Siddhaṃ, Dunhuang finds, apocrypha, and the canon’s Nestorian/Manichaean corner.

groups.heading: Japanese continued commentaries 續經疏部
groups.gloss: 28 vols — not in the CBETA dataset

zones.name: Kangyur
zones.subtitle: bka’ ’gyur · the word of the Buddha
zones.blurb: The translated word of the Buddha — sūtras and tantras. Large tracts are readable via 84000 (open-access, CC BY-NC-ND — free to read, not public domain), so they colour amber.

zones.name: Tengyur
zones.subtitle: bstan ’gyur · the translated treatises
zones.blurb: The greatest library of Indian Buddhist philosophy — Nāgārjuna, Asaṅga, Vasubandhu, Dharmakīrti, Śāntideva. ~99% untranslated; the public-domain islands are a handful of Victorian/early-20th-c. Sanskritists. Internal section boundaries are approximate (≈).
